dimensions.note: Two articles read in full ('매매(賣買)' on buying/selling, '디폴트, 기본값이 아니라고?' on default) both open on a familiar scene or a familiar-but-wrong reading of the target word before naming the economic concept. '매매' opens by naming the everyday native-Korean verb 사고팔다 before introducing the 한자어 매매, then explains the 한자 by decomposing each character into a concrete pictographic story (물건이 나가는 모습, 그물에 담는 모습) rather than a dictionary gloss. '디폴트' opens by voicing the reader's likely wrong guess (컴퓨터를 기본값으로 되돌리는 것) and a concrete scene of a friend borrowing money and refusing to repay, then corrects to the financial sense (채무불이행) via the same 한자 decomposition move. This is the audience-level trait worth carrying: name a concrete, already-known scene or word first, let the reader's existing guess surface (including a plausible wrong one), then attach the technical term to it — never introduce the term cold.
dimensions.evidence: '매매' article: "'팔 매'(賣), '살 매'(買). 우리말 표현인 '사고팔다'라는 말이 더 익숙할 거예요." — '디폴트' article poses the reader's likely misreading before correcting it: "뭔가 전산 문제가 있어 기본값으로 되돌렸다는 뜻일까요?"

dimensions.note: '물가 오르는데 경기까지 침체되나요?' (on stagflation) is written as direct Q&A addressed to the child reader, and the answer is hedged rather than flattened to a flat yes: the piece answers with a stated probability, not a certainty, before walking through the mechanism (rate rises pulling back investment). This is the specific behaviour the audience profile and the constitution both require: simplifying the register must not simplify the epistemic status of the claim. Worth extracting as its own trait, separate from the concreteness trait above, because a piece could get concreteness right and still flatten uncertainty.
dimensions.evidence: "Q. 우리 경제가 나빠지나요? A. 그럴 가능성이 높아요." — hedged (가능성이 높아요), not asserted as settled fact.

dimensions.note: This is a dedicated children's newspaper, so its house genre conventions (Q&A boxes, a recurring 한자어 word-of-the-day column, a running family cast) are its own institutional format, not evidence about how 'news' or 'note' as content types should register a child audience generically. The transferable finding is scoped to audience-suitability above, not to content-type-fit.

strengths: Concrete/familiar-word-first sequencing: names the everyday native-Korean word or the reader's most likely (even if wrong) guess before attaching the technical 한자어 term to it, rather than defining the term cold.

한자어 decomposition as an explanation device: breaks a Sino-Korean economic term into its component characters and gives each a concrete, visualisable origin-story rather than a dictionary paraphrase — this both explains the word and anchors it in something the reader can picture.

Uncertainty survives simplification: a Q&A-format answer to a genuinely uncertain economic question is hedged ('가능성이 높아요') rather than rounded to a flat yes/no, even though the surrounding register is fully child-plain.
weaknesses: The recurring family-character device and the '동화경제'/'시사용어' column formats are this outlet's own recognizable house structure; adopting the underlying concreteness and hedging moves is fine, but reproducing the column format or character names would be imitation, not craft transfer — do_not_copy, not adopt.

Only two articles were read in full (out of a much larger archive); the traits above are corroborated twice within this single source, not yet against an independent institution at the time this record was written — that independent corroboration is what the paired holdout record (ref:bok-easy-economics-elementary) is for.
notes: This record is evidence about the child-upper-elementary AUDIENCE (editorial/profiles/audience/child-upper-elementary.json), not about a genre — the traits (concrete-before-abstract sequencing, 고유어-before-한자어 term introduction, hedged uncertainty) are meant to compose with whatever content type a child-facing piece actually is (a news brief, a report explainer), not to define a 'children's magazine' register. applicable_to.audiences now lists 'child-upper-elementary' first, per SUE-604 correction: this is the audience this corpus is actually evidence about; 'beginner-learner' is retained second only because the 고유어-before-한자어 term-introduction move and the hedging-under-simplification move plausibly transfer to an adult novice too, not because the record's primary scope is adult. Doing so requires schemas/reference-evaluation.schema.json's applicability.audiences enum to admit 'child-upper-elementary' (it does not yet, as of this writing) — flagging again for the Manager to extend the pinned vocabulary as part of SUE-607/SUE-604; until that lands this record is not schema-valid and the Manager should apply the enum change in the same pass as the catalog merge. Simplifying language must never simplify a fact or drop stated uncertainty (editorial/constitution.md §1-3); the hedging finding above is the positive case of that rule holding under real audience adaptation. No article body was reproduced beyond the single-sentence fragments quoted as evidence, consistent with editorial/RIGHTS-AND-PROVENANCE.md's fail-to-reference rule.
